title: Patent Thickets Blocking Cumulative Innovation
bottleneck: Dense overlapping patents in areas like semiconductors, biotech, and software force innovators to navigate licensing minefields, with patent assertion entities taxing productive firms. Defensive patenting consumes R&D budgets that could fund research, and thickets deter small entrants most. Small firms and university spinouts bear the highest costs, entrenching incumbents who can afford patent arsenals.
why_it_blocks: When using an idea requires negotiating with dozens of rights-holders, cumulative innovation stalls. Innovation slows most where it is needed most: among new entrants with fresh ideas.
current_state: Reform efforts (patent quality initiatives, anti-troll legislation) have had limited effect; thickets keep growing. Defensive patent pools and pledges help in narrow domains but do not fix the systemic problem. Targeted patent reform could unlock significant follow-on innovation.
